Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

enable verb

make it possible for someone

also make possible, make it possible, give the chance, thanks to

classical

Caes. BG 1.32: quod reliquīs fugae facultās darētur (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Font. 22: nē īrātō facultās ad dīcendum data esse videātur (Lewis & Short)

facultātem dare

phrase: the person in the dative, what he can do in the genitive (a noun or a gerund) or with ad and the gerund

give the means or the chance

Facultās is the possibility or the means of doing something; it also means ability, skill (dīcendī facultās, eloquence) and, in the plural, means, wealth (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • operā meā, tuā — thanks to me, to you; through my, your doing

    phrase: ablative of <span lang="la">opera</span> with a possessive or a genitive · also used · classical · Cic. Sen. 11: meā operā, Q. Fabī, Tarentum recēpistī (Lewis & Short)

    Says whose help made a thing possible, and also whose fault it was: nōn meā operā … ēvēnit, “it was not my doing” (Ter. Hec. 2.1.31, Lewis & Short).

  • efficiō, efficere, effēcī, effectum — bring it about (that someone can)

    verb, third conjugation (-iō): ut and the subjunctive, here of <span lang="la">possum</span> · also used · classical · Cic. Lael. 59 (Lewis & Short)

    efficere ut possit spells out “enable”; see cause and ensure. For permission, “let”, see allow.

Examples

  • quod reliquīs fugae facultās darētur

    because the rest were given the chance to escapeCaes. BG 1.32 (Lewis & Short)

  • meā operā, Q. Fabī, Tarentum recēpistī

    it was thanks to me, Quintus Fabius, that you got Tarentum backCic. Sen. 11 (Lewis & Short)

  • Tuā operā hoc perficere potuī.

    Thanks to you I was able to finish this.composed

See also allow, cause, ensure, help.

SourcesLewis & Short: facultas · Lewis & Short: opera · Lewis & Short: efficio
